text:
The land use plan of the Village of Olympia Fields also includes a proposed park area with a civic center along Butterfield Creek, running parallel to Lincoln Highway, but several hundred feet north of the highway and this would not be affected. This land is presently owned by the Village of Olympia Fields. If it is developed as a park, the proposed improvement would facilitate access to the parkland.
The Illinois Central Gulf Railroad Station (221st Street) at the intersection of Olympian Way and Lincoln Highway in the Village of Olympia Fields is being studied by the Illinois Department of Transportation - Northeast Region. This project consists of reconstructing the existing parking facility located in the northwest and southwest quadrants of the intersection and will include a bicycle parking area, a taxi parking area, a bus terminal and 325 parking spaces. About ½ acre of additional land to the north of the present facility will be included in this project.
In a letter dated August 14, 1973, from the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission , the following was stated:
"The Commission, through its Planning Committee, found the proposed project to be conditionally consistent with comprehensive regional planning. While the Committee recommended that the Illinois Department of Transportation will be allowed to proceed with the acquisition of land and design approval for the project, actual construction is not to take place until a receipt of affirmative findings has been obtained from the Park Forest Consolidation Study."
Recently, the Park Forest Station Consolidation Study was cancelled by the Village of Park Forest. (Village of Park Forest Resolution No. R-74-12) The Metropolitan Clearinghouse (Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission) was notified that the special condition no longer exists in a letter dated March 21, 1974.
This improvement (Park'n'Ride) would be a separate construction contract developed in accordance with current Federal Highway Administration Policy and Procedures.
At a meeting of the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission held on May 8, 1974 the Commission, through its Planning Committee found the proposed project to be consistent with regional planning policies as set forth in the Comprehensive General Plan and with currently adopted Commission plans and programs.
